title: Long multiplication
keyIdea: Multiply by each digit of the second number separately, then add the rows.

kid: To work out 34 × 26, split 26 into 20 and 6. First 34 × 6 = 204. Then 34 × 20 = 680. Add them: 204 + 680 = 884.
Line the digits up in columns. The second row is for the tens, so it is ten times bigger and ends in a 0.
adult: Long multiplication uses the distributive law: 346 × 27 = 346 × 20 + 346 × 7. Write each partial product on its own row, then add: 6,920 + 2,422 = 9,342.
Two checks catch most mistakes. Estimate first: 346 × 27 is about 350 × 30 = 10,500, so 9,342 is believable. And make sure the tens row has its placeholder 0.

familyTip: Before you multiply, round both numbers and estimate. After you multiply, compare your answer with the estimate.

practice.hint: Multiply by the ones digit, then by the tens, then add the two rows.

practice.explain: The 3 in 34 means 30, and 52 × 30 = 1560, which ends in 0.
